title: ork accepts slicer relay v11
lead: ork accepts slicer relay v11, its role prompts follow v11's rules, and it reads the gate role from v11's JSON and records the gate verdict instead of special-casing the gate.
findings_note: owner contract review 2026-10-30 (slicer, adj, ork alignment); slicer s424 (relay v11 cleanup and bump)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the contract pins (S24), adj's JSON contract (adjudicate S45), serving or translating an older contract, any change to slicer, and the engine's v11 process rules (small-fix recheck by the raising role, one-pass regate after a clean merge, [AFTER LAND] Check lines, non-blocker owner questions, `counts.roles`), which are S204.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
slicer v1.17 bumps the relay contract to v11 (`../slicer` s424, which lands after s391, s407, s409 and s412). ork accepts only v9 and v10 (`internal/roles/roles.go`, `acceptedContracts`), so engine start and doctor refuse a project once its slicer prints v11 (`internal/cli/upgrade.go`, `internal/engine/engine.go`). Owner decision 2026-10-30: one v11 bump in slicer v1.17, with this companion slice in ork.

**Blocked on slicer s424 landing.** The golden and the exact rule text come from its output; until it lands, re-read `slicer ai relay --json` from `../slicer` main and the final `RELAY_CHANGES` entry for 11 before claiming.

v11 changes ork must follow (as planned in s424; confirm against the landed text):

- No `cd` for every role, the read-only ones included; a resumed headless role runs in the slice worktree (slicer s391).
- Implementer re-anchors cited lines and runs a defect self-check before review: concurrency and handle lifetime, docs updated with the code, a test that fails when the wiring is removed (slicer s407). `prompts/implementer.md` already re-anchors; add the self-check.
- A small fix round may be re-checked by whichever read-only role holds the findings; non-blocking owner questions are asked as they arise; parallel slices gate once on the merged result (slicer s412, as settled there).
- A `blocker` owner question is a wait, not a stop: it leaves `stop[]`. `stop[]` entries gain keys. `roles[]` gains `gate` with `ledger_role` `gate` (slicer s424).

Alignment gap found in the same review: ork's engine falls back to the next row on an exit classified `error` (S169 notes: a Claude limit shows as `error`), while the v10 `vendor_limit` obligation says any failure other than a classified limit stops. Owner decision 2026-10-30: the contract follows ork. slicer s424 widens the v11 fallback to an error exit of the agent process, so ork's existing behaviour conforms and needs no change; confirm against the landed text, and follow the conformance key if s424 renames it (`vendor_limit` to `role_fallback`, say).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/roles/roles.go:36,57`: `ContractVersion = 11`; `acceptedContracts = {10, 11}`. v9 is dropped (adj 175, `boundary.contract-set`, decided 2026-10-30); the comment cites it.
- `internal/roles/prompts/*.md`: first line `relay v11`, plus the v11 rules that are a role's own: no `cd` for every role, the implementer's defect self-check (concurrency and handle lifetime, docs updated in the same diff, a test that fails when the new wiring is removed), the gate fails on every `fix` finding (no severity; a minor item is `later`), the gate closes its round with a verdict.
- `internal/slicercli/contract.go:16-61,63-108`: decode `stop[]` as `{key, text}` entries (a v10 contract's plain strings still decode); for v11 require the conformance keys `role_fallback` and `blocker_wait` (v10 keeps `vendor_limit`) and `gate` in `roles[]`; `LedgerRole("gate")` reads the contract when `roles[]` has it and keeps the v10 special case otherwise. Owner decision 2026-10-30: `stop[]` keys are decoded, not required.
- `internal/slicercli/write.go:132-139`: `StepSpec` gains a verdict and `RelayStep` sends `--verdict pass|fail` (slicer 1.17.0: `relay-run step --phase done --verdict`).
- `internal/engine/round.go:438` (`stepEnd`) and `internal/engine/states.go:556`: a gate round closes with `--phase done --verdict pass|fail` when the run's recorded contract is v11; v10 closes as today (a v10 slicer may lack the flag). The implementer re-anchors the exact spot.
- `internal/cli/upgrade.go:161` messages if the accepted set's wording changes, and the older-than message test.
- `testdata/cli/slicer/relay-v11.json` recorded from `slicer ai relay --json` (slicer 1.17.0 is installed; decision 0047); keep `relay-v10.json`.
- `testdata/roles/relay-first-line.txt`, `testdata/roles/relay-orchestrator-first-line.txt`: first line `relay v11`.
- Docs that name the version: `docs/boundaries.md:35-43`, `docs/design.md:668,807-809,1422-1428` (809 calls falling back on a plain error exit a deviation from v10; v11's `role_fallback` follows ork, so say so), `docs/glossary.md:9,145-146`, `docs/orchestrator-parity.md:186`, `AGENTS.md:105`, CHANGELOG. `docs/guide.md` names no version and stays as is.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `CheckContractLine("Contract: relay v11")` returns 11 with no error; v9 and v12 are refused and the message names {10, 11}.
- `RelayContract.Validate` accepts the recorded v11 JSON; refuses v11 JSON with no `gate` in `roles[]`, with no `role_fallback` conformance key, or with no `blocker_wait` key; still accepts the recorded v10 JSON (plain-string `stop[]`, `vendor_limit`).
- The recorded v11 JSON decodes `stop[]` to `gate_fail_3`, `spec_wrong`, `permission_denied`, `no_eligible_row`, in that order, each with text.
- `LedgerRole("gate")` on the recorded v11 JSON reads its `ledger_role`; on v10 it returns `gate`.
- Each prompt's first line equals `relay v11` (the existing first-line tests and `testdata/roles/*first-line.txt`, retargeted).
- The implementer prompt names the three self-check categories; each role prompt forbids `cd`; the gate prompt fails on every `fix` finding.
- With a fake slicer printing v11, a gate PASS closes its step with `--phase done --verdict pass` and a gate FAIL with `--verdict fail`; with v10, neither flag is sent.
- Engine start with a fake slicer printing v11 creates a run; with v12 or v9 it refuses naming the accepted set.
- The upgrade message test for an older-than version names the new set.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Record `relay-v11.json` from the installed slicer 1.17.0 (`slicer ai relay --json`) and read its `RELAY_CHANGES` entry for 11 (`changes[]`, last entry).
2. The accepted-set decision is adj 175 (`boundary.contract-set`, decided). Cite it; do not record it again.
3. Write the red tests against the recorded output, then the code and prompts.
4. Update the docs listed in Files. Refer to slicer's commands; do not paste its contract text.
5. The engine's v11 process rules are S204. If a prompt change needs one of them, report it; do not build it here.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are clean. SPDX headers. No new dependency.
- `slicer check` and `adj lint` pass.
- [HUMAN CHECK] With slicer v1.17 installed, `ork doctor` is ok and one relay runs end to end on a scratch project.
